summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with HLA-B27-positive ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, obesity, asthma, and obstructive sleep apnea, was admitted for an acute flare of left sacroiliac joint pain that severely limited his mobility and prevented him from leaving home. He reported symptoms consistent with prior flares and denied trauma, fever, or neurological changes. Due to concerns about radiation exposure, imaging was declined. He received IV hydromorphone and ketorolac for breakthrough pain and was started on a short prednisone taper based on rheumatology input, as he had previously responded well to steroids. His pain improved, and he was discharged home with a 3-day opioid supply to bridge until his outpatient prescription could be refilled. He was advised to continue all home medications, including the steroid taper, asthma inhalers, CPAP, and lisinopril. Follow-up was recommended with his primary care provider.
